translationRepairs: Then there were exemplars such as the wife of Liang Hong, who shared her husband's seclusion without complaint, and Gong Jiang, who swore never to enter a second household—models of wifely duty and maternal virtue celebrated in the histories; these represent an even higher standard.

Then there were exemplars such as the wife of Liang Hong, who shared her husband's seclusion without complaint, and Gong Jiang, who swore never to enter a second household—models of wifely duty and maternal virtue celebrated in the histories; these too are among their strengths.
其次 introduces a second exemplary type after the martyrs, and 又其長也 marks these as a further excellence, not a higher standard than death-defying loyalty.
Pei Shi, wife of Li Dewu—Pei Shi, styled Shuying, was the daughter of Pei Ju, Director of the Household Ministry and Duke of Anyi.
Pei Shi, wife of Li Dewu, was styled Shuying and was the daughter of Pei Ju, Director of the Household Ministry and Duke of Anyi.
The Chinese names 裴氏 once, then 字淑英 and her father; the em-dash restatement invents a second Pei Shi not present in the source.
She married Li Dewu, but after only a year he was banished to Lingnan because of his cousin Jin Cai's case.
She married Li Dewu, but after only a year he was banished to Lingnan because of his paternal uncle Jin Cai's case.
從父 is a paternal uncle, so 坐從父金才事 cannot be rendered as cousin Jin Cai's case.
When the Taizong besieged Luoyang, Qing plotted to turn against Shichong and wished to come over to the Tang together with his wife.
When Taizong besieged Luoyang, Qing plotted to turn against Shichong and wished to come over to the Tang together with his wife.
太宗 is the temple name Taizong; the English article in “the Taizong” is ungrammatical and is not licensed by the Chinese.
Li Shi, wife of Yang San'an—Li Shi was a native of Jingyang in Yongzhou.
Li Shi, wife of Yang San'an, was a native of Jingyang in Yongzhou.
楊三安妻李氏 is a single identification followed by native place; the em-dash repeats Li Shi as if a second clause.
By day Li worked the fields; by night she spun and wove; within several years she buried her parents-in-law and seven of her husband's uncles, nephews, and brothers—deeply admired near and far.

By day Li worked the fields; by night she spun and wove; within several years she conducted seven funerals for her parents-in-law and her husband's uncles, nephews, and brothers—deeply admired near and far.
者七喪 totals seven funerals covering 舅姑 and 夫之叔侄兄弟, not seven extra agnates besides the parents-in-law.
Wang Shi, wife of Wei Heng—Wang Shi was a native of Qi in Zizhou.
Wang Shi, wife of Wei Heng, was a native of Qi in Zizhou.
魏衡妻王氏 is named once before the native-place clause; the em-dash restatement doubles Wang Shi.
Jing Shi, mother of Fan Huiren—Jing Shi, styled Xiangzi, was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
Jing Shi, mother of Fan Huiren, was styled Xiangzi and was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
The duplicated Jing Shi should be removed, but “mother of Fan Huiren, styled Xiangzi” can attach 字像子 to the son; the courtesy name belongs to 敬氏.
At the slightest hint of persuasion she would weep in grief and resentment; this happened four times.
At the slightest hint of persuasion she would weep in grief and resentment; this happened again and again.
如此者數四 is an iterative “again and again,” not a count of exactly four occasions.
The Filial Daughter Jia of Puzhou—the Filial Daughter Jia was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
The Filial Daughter Jia of Puzhou was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
The chapter lemma repeats 孝女賈氏, but received editions identify one woman; English should not treat the splice as two subjects.
Lu Shi, wife of Zheng Yizong—Lu Shi was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou, daughter of Lu Yanheng.
Lu Shi, wife of Zheng Yizong, was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou and daughter of Lu Yanheng.
鄭義宗妻盧氏 is one subject of native place and parentage; the em-dash restatement doubles Lu Shi.
At eighteen Shangguan married Prince Lingui, succeeding as consort after the lamented King of Chu.
At eighteen Shangguan married Prince Lingui, who succeeded in the line of King Ai of Chu.
哀王 is the posthumous title Ai, not “lamented,” but the proposed participle still makes Shangguan the successor; 繼楚哀王後 describes 靈龜’s succession.
She married the Duke of Yanshou, son of Qinming, to Minzhi.
She married Minzhi, son of Qinming, Duke of Yanshou.
適延壽公於欽明子敏直 means she married Minzhi, son of Yu Qinming, Duke of Yanshou; the original reverses the spouse.
Xi Shi, wife of Zou Baoying—Xi Shi; her place of origin is unknown.
Xi Shi, wife of Zou Baoying; her place of origin is unknown.
奚氏 is named once before 不知何許人也; the em-dash repeats Xi Shi without a second Chinese clause.
Wei Shi, wife of Song Tingyu—Wei Shi was a native of Gucheng in Dingzhou, descendant of the Sui Authoring Gentleman Yanquan.
Wei Shi, wife of Song Tingyu, was a native of Gucheng in Dingzhou, descendant of the Sui Authoring Gentleman Yanquan.
The lemma splice repeats 宋庭瑜妻魏氏, but the biography is one identification plus native place and ancestry, not two persons.
Her father Xian enjoyed a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Assistant of the Ministry of Works.
Her father Xian enjoyed a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Assistant of the Wenchang (Department of State Affairs).
文昌左丞 is the Zhou title for Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs (Wenchang), not the Ministry of Works.
Her father Xian had a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Assistant of the Ministry of Works.
Her father Xian had a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Assistant of the Wenchang (Department of State Affairs).
The same office error appears in the literal line: 文昌左丞 is Wenchang Left Assistant, not Ministry of Works.
On the eve of the wedding they were about to tell Lu;
Only on the eve of the wedding did they tell Lu;
方以告盧 marks the moment they did tell her, not that they were still about to tell her.
Jingzhao Assistant Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody in their praise.
Jingzhao Prefect Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody in their praise.
京兆尹 is Jingzhao Prefect (Yin), the same office already rendered Prefect for 第五琦, not Assistant.
Jingzhao Assistant Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody to praise them.
Jingzhao Prefect Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody to praise them.
京兆尹 is Jingzhao Prefect, not Assistant, in the literal line as well.
At the time Cao Sheng was promoted to Prefect of Xuzhou; learning the bandits had surrendered, he led troops in a surprise attack.
At the time Cao Sheng served as Prefect of Xuzhou; learning the bandits had surrendered, he led troops in a surprise attack.
任徐州刺史 records tenure in office, not a promotion.

縣尉 is the county defender/assistant magistrate, distinct from 令; both Lu Fu and Wang Fan are 尉, not magistrates.
His wife was then bound to a tree by the rebels, cut apart, and eaten; to the end she called to her husband, "Serve Vice Censor Wu well."
His wife was then bound to a tree by the rebels, cut apart, and eaten; to the end she called to her husband, "Serve Pushe Wu well."
烏僕射 addresses Wu as Pushe (Vice Director), not Vice Censor (御史).
Changling often served as Chief Administrator of Si Prefecture and his family had dwelt in Cai for generations.
Changling had been Chief Administrator of Si Prefecture and his family had dwelt in Cai for generations.
常為泗州長史 marks a prior posting (常/嘗), not habitual “often served.”
He served Wu Shaocheng and Shaoyang in succession; by Yuanji's time he was Magistrate of Wu Fang.
He served Wu Shaocheng and Shaoyang in succession; by Yuanji's time he was Magistrate of Wufang.
吳房 is the county name Wufang, not two words Wu Fang.
Xianzong heard with joy and urgently summoned Changling to court, directly appointing him Magistrate of Yancheng and Acting Investigating Censor, and granting the scarlet robe and fish tally.
Xianzong heard with joy and urgently summoned Changling to court, directly appointing him Magistrate of Yancheng and concurrent Investigating Censor, and granting the scarlet robe and fish tally.
兼監察御史 is concurrent tenure; 攝 would be acting, as later for Wei Yong.
When Zhang Hongjing governed Youzhou, he memorialized and appointed Yong Observation Aide, acting as Investigating Censor.
When Zhang Hongjing governed Youzhou, he memorialized and appointed him Observation Aide, acting as Investigating Censor.
奏授觀察判官 appoints him Observation Aide; “Yong Observation Aide” fuses the personal name 雍 into the office.
Fanghou, in the Taihe era served as Recorder of Yong Regional Commandery; he was falsely accused and killed by Pacification Commissioner Dong Changling.
Fanghou, in the Taihe era served as Recorder of the Yongzhou Area Command; he was falsely accused and killed by Pacification Commissioner Dong Changling.
邕州都督府 is the Yongzhou (邕) area-command headquarters, not Yong in the 永 sense.
